role: Lecturer, then associate professor of political science; chair of the Department of Political Studies and Public Administration (2005–2007)
organization: American University of Beirut; Takla Law Firm
description: Resumed legal practice at the Takla firm and teaching of international law and international relations at AUB; associate professor of political science from 2005 and department chair from 2005 until he took leave in 2007 to become UN ambassador.

Secretary-General of the commission charged with drafting a new electoral law for Lebanon. He also sat on the Executive Bureau of the Economic and Social Council (1999–2002) and the Lebanese National Commission for UNESCO (2000–2004).

role: Ambassador and Permanent Representative of Lebanon to the United Nations
organization: Permanent Mission of Lebanon to the United Nations, New York
description: Represented Lebanon during its 2010–2011 term on the UN Security Council, holding the Council's rotating presidency in May 2010 and September 2011, and was a Vice-President of the 67th session of the General Assembly (2012–2013). His interventions focused on Resolution 1701 and southern Lebanon and on the Special Tribunal for Lebanon on the assassination of Rafic Hariri.

Elected by the UN General Assembly and Security Council on 9 November 2017 for a nine-year term from 6 February 2018, the second Lebanese judge on the Court after Fouad Ammoun. He resigned on 14 January 2025, two years before his term was due to end, after being named Prime Minister.

Elected President by his fellow judges for three years. He presided over proceedings including South Africa v. Israel (provisional-measures orders of March and May 2024), the advisory opinion of 19 July 2024 on Israel's policies in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and Nicaragua v. Germany. See polemics for the criticism this drew from Israeli officials.

role: Prime Minister (President of the Council of Ministers)
description: Named Prime Minister-designate on 13 January 2025 with 84 of 128 MPs; his 24-minister government was formed on 8 February 2025 and won parliament's confidence on 26 February 2025 (95 votes). In office as of October 2026.
